# Propuesta: Superchain Risk Layer + OP Enterprise para Optimism / OP Labs

**Fecha:** 2026-11-22  
**Target:** Optimism / OP Labs — ethereum-optimism/optimism  
**Canal:** GitHub Issue técnico + email partnerships@oplabs.xyz  
**Autor:** CloudBuilder (IVANLI2412)

---

## Resumen

**Superchain Risk Layer** — Capa de riesgo unificada para toda la Superchain (OP Mainnet, Base, Mode, Fraxtal, Zora, Lyra, etc.): cross-chain bridge monitoring, fault proof health, sequencer decentralization tracking, governance risk scoring. **OP Enterprise Toolkit** — SDK + dashboard para teams deployando en Superchain: pre-deploy audit, gas optimization, compliance checks.

**Presupuesto:** $100,000–$200,000 USDC (OP Grants / RetroPGF / Enterprise)  
**Duración:** 4 meses  
**Licencia:** MIT

---

## Problema

La Superchain crece (>15 chains, >$5B TVL) pero **riesgo fragmentado por chain**:

- Bridge risk entre L2s (SuperchainERC20, third-party) no unificado
- Fault proof system (Cannon) health no visible a developers
- Sequencer decentralization roadmap — sin tracking público
- Governance risk (OP token, voting, upgrades) no cuantificado
- Teams enterprise necesitan compliance pre-deploy (SOC2, audit trails)

---

## Solución: Superchain Risk Layer + OP Enterprise

### Risk Layer (Infra pública, open source)

| Componente | Función | Data Source |
|------------|---------|-------------|
| **Cross-Chain Bridge Monitor** | Canonical (Optimism Portal) + 3rd party (Wormhole, LayerZero, Axelar) | RPC + Subgraphs + Hyperlane |
| **Fault Proof Health** | Cannon challenger status, bond health, dispute game metrics | OP Stack contracts |
| **Sequencer Decentralization Tracker** | Leader election, proposer set, forced inclusion SLAs | Sequencer RPC + contracts |
| **Governance Risk Oracle** | OP token concentration, proposal analysis, upgrade timelocks | Snapshot + Tally + contracts |
| **Unified Risk API** | `/v1/superchain/risk/{chainId}` — Score 0-100 + breakdown | REST + WebSocket + x402 |

### OP Enterprise Toolkit (B2B)

- `op-risk audit <repo>` — Pre-deploy security + gas + compliance
- `op-risk simulate <tx>` — Cross-chain simulation, gas estimate
- `op-risk monitor` — Alertas Slack/Discord/Webhook + x402
- Dashboard enterprise: `enterprise.optimism.cloudbuilder.dev`

---

## Diferenciadores CloudBuilder

1. **Superchain-native** — Primer tool que agrupa riesgo cross-L2
2. **x402 + OP Stack aligned** — Low fees = micro-payments viables
3. **Motor C** — Auto-contribuye a awesome-optimism/superchain-tools
4. **Production stack** — pumpfun-quant-ai: isolated signer, risk veto, memory

---

## Roadmap (4 meses)

| Mes | Hito | Entregable |
|-----|------|------------|
| 1 | Bridge indexer + Fault proof health | API riesgo cross-chain 5+ L2s |
| 2 | Sequencer tracker + Governance oracle | Risk score unificado 15 chains |
| 3 | Enterprise SDK + x402 gateway | CLI + Dashboard beta |
| 4 | OP Grants report + 3 enterprise pilots | $10K+ ARR pipeline |

---

## Métricas éxito

- 15/15 Superchain chains monitoreadas
- 1,000+ API calls/día (risk layer)
- 3 enterprise pilots firmados
- $25,000+ USDC volumen x402 + enterprise

---

## Equipo

- **Iván Zenteno** — OP Stack, Rust indexers, x402, enterprise sales
- **Stack:** pumpfun-quant-ai (reutiliza risk engine, memory, x402 pro)

---

## Presupuesto

| Concepto | USDC |
|----------|------|
| Desarrollo (4 meses × 1.5 FTE) | 80,000 |
| Indexing infra (RPC, subgraphs, Workers) | 20,000 |
| Enterprise sales / pilot onboarding | 30,000 |
| Auditoría + compliance review | 20,000 |
| Buffer | 20,000 |
| **Total** | **170,000** |

---

## Contacto

- **GitHub:** https://github.com/IVANLI2412/pumpfun-quant-ai
- **Demo:** `http://localhost:8000/v1/services` (x402 endpoints live)
- **Wallet:** `CnX1DZTzyFH8u1o2NFEgVcLakaZazT5ZzPDpqUb2AsAo` (OP Mainnet / Base)

---

topPRs.title: kona-engine,kona-node!: never move the safe head above the previous safe head on a reset
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
Stacked on #23859 (base `joshklop/kona-reset-epoch`), so the diff shows only this change. Stack, in merge order: #23990 → #23883 → #23859 → **this PR**.

On an engine reset (any restart, an invalid forkchoice response, or an admin reset), kona-node could pick a safe head above the previous safe head. That happened whenever derivation lagged the unsafe chain by more than a sequence window. The reset then labelled safe blocks that derivation never checked against L1, and derivation resumed above them, so they were never checked at all. There are two ways to get there:
- **The batches were never posted**, for example with the batcher down for longer than a window. Derivation from L1 replaces those blocks with deposit-only blocks, so kona's safe head is on the wrong chain.
- **The batches are on L1, but derivation is behind.** This happens when a verifier catches up after downtime while gossip keeps its unsafe head current, or when derivation stalls. The labelled blocks are usually the batched ones, but the safe head database records them under L1 blocks they were not derived from. If gossip and the batches differ, as after an unsafe reorg or a conductor failover, the blocks are also wrong.

A reset now chooses the safe head as op-node's `FindL2Heads` does. It never moves the safe head above the execution layer's safe label, and it restarts from the end of an epoch at least a sequence window behind the highest block with a canonical L1 origin.

It also ports `FindL2Heads`'s two early recoveries. They apply when safe and finalized are still at genesis more than 14 sequence windows after it, or when the unsafe head is below safe or finalized. Safe and finalized then go `--syncmode.offset-el-safe` behind the unsafe head. Without the first, a sequencer whose execution layer synced without finality would walk every block back to genesis on its reset, because #23883 covers only verifiers. That is the ordering hazard from ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#589.

A reset after a long derivation stall now walks back to the previous safe head, one L2 block per RPC. After three days without batches on OP Mainnet that is about 130k blocks instead of about 22k. op-node walks the same blocks.

`SyncLookback` stays the sequence window: kona-node refuses alt-DA chains at startup, so the alt-DA part of the issue does not apply.

`TestRestartKeepsUnderivedBlocksUnsafe` covers the derivation-behind case. An op-node and a kona-node verifier derive only from L1 blocks 24 deep, with a sequencing window of 8. Each one's CL restarts, and the test checks that the safe head never has an L1 origin shallower than derivation can reach. Without the fix, kona-node's reset labels block 52 safe with L1 origin 33 on L1 head 45, and the test fails. The test passes on both clients with the fix.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/575

**Review findings dismissed, for the author to confirm:**
- *Start the safe walk at the previous safe head to skip the blocks above it.* Kept op-node's block-by-block walk, because nothing checks that the EL's safe label is an ancestor of its unsafe head. The per-block log is now `debug!` instead.
- *Move the recovery predicates onto `L2ForkchoiceState`, and share test helpers between `mod.rs` and `el_sync.rs`.* Left as is to keep the diff focused.
- *safedb:* in the recovery paths, the offset head is read from the EL. If the database already reaches that height, it is re-recorded at an existing L1 key without a hash check. op-node's reset does the same. A hash check would clear the database on a mismatch, as `safeDBRefAfterELSync` does.
- *Sequencer during EL sync:* kona's sequencer resets at startup unconditionally, while op-node skips that reset during initial EL sync. If the execution layer is part-way through EL sync and already more than 14 sequence windows in, the lost-labels recovery sets finalized behind that partial tip. `reset_after_el_sync` then sees finality and skips the offset step. Labels end up lower than needed, which is a liveness issue only. This is the sequencer gap already noted in #23883.

- *Acceptance test:*
  - The test starts both CL kinds itself, so it runs in both the op-node and kona-node CI jobs. This matches `derivation/confirmations` and keeps op-node as the reference.
  - Its `awaitStatus` helper copies the one in `derivation/confirmations` instead of moving it to the DSL.
  - Until op-node sees its first L1 head after a restart, its confirmation depth is not applied (`confdepth.go`). Locally it saw the head about 100 ms after starting, before derivation began.

BREAKING CHANGE: `find_starting_forkchoice` takes the `--syncmode.offset-el-safe` duration as a third argument. After a reset that follows a derivation stall, kona-node's safe head is now at or below its previous safe head, so safe progress restarts further back.

topPRs.title: op-devstack,kona-node-rpc: run follow_l2 and no-supernode interop tests on kona-node
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
The kona-node acceptance job never ran kona-node as the follow_l2 sequencer or follow source, and it skipped every interop test that runs without a supernode, because those presets pinned or only started op-node. kona-node replaces op-node, so these are gaps in the coverage it needs before then. This PR closes them:

- **follow_l2**: the sequencer, the deriving verifier and the follower all run on `DEVSTACK_L2CL_KIND`. Each test also runs with the follow source on the other CL, so the op-node job now checks op-node following kona-node, and the kona-node job keeps checking kona-node following op-node.
- **No-supernode interop**: the kona-node job now runs `upgrade-no-supervisor` (2 tests), `super-opnode` (2) and the `l2cl` cases of four `TestZK_HonestChallenger` tests. They source super roots from kona-node's `superroot_atTimestamp`.

Running them exposed a kona-node gap: it did not serve `optimism_dependencySet`, which op-node serves and the op-test-sequencer reads on any chain with Lagoon scheduled. kona-node now serves it, with op-node's plain `not found` error when it runs without a dependency set. This is the only user-facing change; the rest is test infrastructure.

Each commit is atomic and the series is meant to be reviewed commit by commit: devstack change, then the tests it enables.

## Notes for reviewers
- One local run in three of the all-kona `TestFollowL2_Safe_Finalized_CurrentL1` timed out: the kona-node sequencer's finalized head stayed 6 blocks behind the kona-node deriving verifier's for a full L1 finality step. The cross-client cases and the op-node job never failed. A separate investigation is under way; if it reproduces in CI, the kona-node job gets a flake from this PR until that lands.
- CI time grows: every follow_l2 test runs two systems in both jobs, and the kona-node job picks up eight interop tests. The kona-node job's `parallelism: 2` comment assumes it is about a third of the op-node job, so check the shard wall times here. Until this merges, the shard split uses develop's timings, which record these tests as skipped or single-system, so a kona-node shard can run long on this PR.
- The `super-opnode` tests and the ZK `op-node` subtests are renamed (`...FromL2CL`, `l2cl`) because they now run against either CL. The package directory keeps its name to avoid churn.

## Reviews
- `go-code-reviewer`, `rust-code-reviewer` and `deletion-reviewer` ran. Applied: the dependency set moves onto `SingleChainInteropSupport` so every CL of an interop chain gets it, an unknown `WithFollowSourceCLKind` fails before any node starts, a shared `plain_error` helper in kona-node-rpc, and an exact-JSON assertion for `optimism_dependencySet`, including `null` for an unset expiry override.
- Dismissed: deciding "runs interop" from the rollup config's Lagoon time rather than `PresetConfig.InteropAtGenesis`. That would also change what op-node starts with on chains that schedule Lagoon through a deployer option, which is out of scope; the doc comment says what it keys on.
- Skipped `interop-reviewer`: no interop message verification or safety logic changes.

Closes #24121
Part of #24122 (its second criterion, a stall test for follow mode, remains open)
Part of ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#101

topPRs.title: kona-engine: read only headers for the super-root output
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
Stacked on #23960 (base `einar/superroot-by-number`); merge that first.

`superroot_atTimestamp` reads the target block with all its transactions to build an `L2BlockInfo`, but an output root only needs the header. On busy chains a full block is megabytes of JSON, which eats into the RPC timeout that #23960 is meant to fit inside. op-node's `OutputV0AtBlock` reads only the header.

`superroot_atTimestamp` now asks the EL only for headers (`eth_getBlockByHash` / `eth_getBlockByNumber` with `false`). Its answers are unchanged. `optimism_outputAtBlock` still reads the full block, because its response needs the L1 origin and sequence number from the L1-info deposit.

If the EL returns a header whose reported hash is not its own hash, the query now fails with an internal error, as op-node's header check does. Before, the block id was computed from the header but the output root used the reported hash. For a block read by number, nothing compared the two, so after Isthmus a mismatch would have been served in the output root.

Reviews: `rust-code-reviewer` found nothing blocking. I applied its point about using one hash and its doc nit. I dismissed its nit to replace the `(id, output)` tuple with a struct, because that shape predates this PR and `output_at_block` shares it. `safedb-reviewer` found nothing that changes when the query answers or which `required_l1` it pairs with the output. Its one finding was the unchecked hash above, which this PR fixes.

Part of #23473.

topPRs.title: op-test-sequencer: return the start error instead of panicking on close
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
When a configured service fails to start, op-test-sequencer now returns that error. Before this change it panicked with a nil-pointer dereference in `work.(*Ensemble).Close`, because each error path in `Ensemble.Start` returned `nil` into the named result that the deferred cleanup closed. The panic hid the real cause of the failure. One acceptance run crashed with SIGSEGV when the actual problem was that the L2 builder could not fetch `optimism_dependencySet`. There is no change when startup succeeds.

The services that already started are still closed, and any close error is joined to the start error. The new tests fail with the original SIGSEGV on the old code. They can't show that the started services are closed, because noop services have no observable `Close` and the config has no way to plug in a test service. I didn't think it was worth adding one for this fix.

`go-code-reviewer` ran. I applied its suggestion to drop a test assertion that didn't prove `Start` closes anything.
